default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: I arrived at school at 8 o’clock.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に follows a noun that indicates a specific time to show when an action takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination or endpoint of a movement action 着く.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past tense, showing that the action has been completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: Both the specific time (8 o’clock) and the destination of the verb 着く use the particle に, and the sentence ends with the past form ました to show that the event was completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle へ emphasizes the direction of movement toward the school rather than the destination itself, as in に.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing the pronunciation of 着く (つく - arrive) with 着る (きる - put on clothes).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: Many animals died because of the typhoon.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で follows a noun referring to a natural disaster to show the cause or reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: This noun-modifying phrase indicates a large quantity of the noun どうぶつ that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject affected by an event or change of state in a natural sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate is in the polite past form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The particle で shows an objective cause related to a natural disaster, while the subject takes が to clarify who suffered the disaster.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: から emphasizes a starting point or a more subjective assumed cause, rather than the direct cause of a natural disaster such as で.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use the particle で for a cause when the following clause expresses intention, a command, or an invitation.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: I stayed at a Japanese-style inn for the first time.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the origin or type of the noun 旅館 that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates a fixed place of lodging and is used with the verb 泊まる.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the verb and emphasizes that it was a first-time experience.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate describes an action of staying at an inn that took place.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The lodging place of the verb 泊まる always takes the particle に, while the adverb はじめて comes before the verb to modify the experience.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle で usually indicates a place where an ordinary activity takes place, while with the verb 泊まる, に is the most accurate particle for indicating a place of lodging.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Avoid mispronouncing 旅館 (りょかん) as ろかん or confusing it with the word 旅行 (りょこう).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: The sky is really beautiful today, isn’t it?
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time きょう the general topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が emphasizes that the subject is the direct object being described.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending な combines with the ending ですね to express emotion and seek agreement.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: Use は to introduce the background topic (today), use が to identify the thing being observed and described (the sky), and end with ですね to create agreement in communication.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Make the phrase “today’s sky” the only main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Note that きれい is an adjective ending in な, not an adjective ending in い.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: Because there was not enough time, I could not do it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the intransitive verb 足りる.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 足りる changes to the negative form て to connect a clause expressing an objective reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the negative potential form in the past tense.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: Use the negative form て (なくて) to connect the cause and result clauses gently and objectively. The following past negative potential form できませんでした shows that the task could not be completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: から emphasizes a more subjective reason and clearer justification than the use of て.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: The verb 足りる is a group 2 verb, so its negative form is 足りない. At beginner level, avoid incorrectly changing it to 足らない.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: I will watch a soccer match with my friends.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と indicates the person who participates in the action together with the subject.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の modifies the noun 試合 that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of watching.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb predicate is in the polite form and describes a future action.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The sentence describes an intended action with a co-participant (友だちと), an affected object (サッカーの試合を), and a verb predicate at the end (見ます).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the particle に indicates an action directed toward a friend, such as meeting or speaking to a friend, rather than doing something together.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle と (doing something with someone) with に (an action directed toward an object).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: As for today, this restaurant is quiet and has empty seats.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.sk: N(time) は + N は + Vています
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the time as the background and topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は emphasizes the subject whose state is being described today.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the form ている indicates that the restaurant is empty and has few customers.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The sentence uses two levels of topics with the particle は (きょうは limits the time, while このレストランは introduces the subject), combined with the predicate Vています to describe the restaurant’s current state.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern has the opposite meaning and describes a crowded restaurant full of people.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing the reading of the kanji 空 in 空[あ]く (empty, with available seats) with 空[そら] (the sky) or the adjective 暇[ひま] (free or available for a person).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to the department store to buy clothes.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.sk: N(time) + N(place) に + N を + V(remove ます) に + 行きました
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This past-time adverb modifies the entire action that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を indicates the object affected by the action of buying.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb without ます combines with the particle に to express the purpose of movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb predicate is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.cn: V(remove ます) / N + に + 行く/来る/帰る
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: The sentence describes purposeful movement using the structure Vに 行きました, together with a past time marker (きのう) and a destination (デパートに).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the present form 行きます indicates a habit or an intention to go shopping, not an action that happened in the past.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Using Vて行きました means buying something and then taking it somewhere, rather than going for the purpose of shopping.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: When using the movement-purpose structure Vに行く, the verb before に must drop the ending ます. Do not use the dictionary form 買うに行く.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies this room as the topic whose feature is being described.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective predicate ending in い combines with です to create a polite tone while describing the topic’s quality.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The sentence directly describes the feature or quality of something. The topic is このへや, combined with the polite adjective predicate ending in い (ひろいです).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This adjective has the opposite meaning, “narrow,” and is used to describe a room with a small, limited area.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: When the adjective ending in い is used with です in the present tense to speak politely, it keeps い unchanged. Do not add な or だ (do not say ひろいだ or ひろいなです).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: The person singing over there is Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.sk: N (place) で + Vている のは + N です
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で identifies the place where the singing action takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb phrase is turned into a noun with の and combined with particle は to make the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun predicate combines with です to confirm the identity of the person being discussed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: The sentence uses the nominalization pattern 'Vているのは Nです' to emphasize information about the subject (たなかさん) of the action taking place at a location (あそこで).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the usual way to describe Mr. Tanaka's action, rather than using a structure that emphasizes the identity of the person who is singing.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Particle の in '〜のは' acts as a nominalizer (replacing a person or thing), so の must not be omitted before particle は.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + N です
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: I do not know what to do, so I am very troubled.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The indirect-question clause serves as the unclear content of the verb わからなくて.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the て form expresses the cause or reason leading to the troubled state in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the ている form describes the speaker's current state of confusion or difficulty.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The sentence expresses a cause-and-effect relationship using the て form (わからなくて). The cause is not knowing how to deal with the situation (どうしたらいいか), and the result is a difficult state (こまっています).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: The conditional form ば has a similar meaning but sounds slightly more formal and written than たら.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Using こまりました refers to a problem that has arisen and put the speaker in a difficult position, while こまっています emphasizes an ongoing state of being stuck.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: When the て form connects a cause-and-effect clause with verbs expressing feelings, such as こまる, the following clause must not contain a request, command, or invitation.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: I said goodbye to my friend in front of the station.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle の connects two nouns and modifies the location word まえ that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle で indicates the place where the farewell took place.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle と indicates the person who took part in the farewell.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb わかれる is in the polite past form ました and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The sentence describes an action in the past. It follows the order of the place of the action (N で), the person involved (N と), and the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using に会う means 'meet a friend' (start a meeting), rather than 'say goodbye / part' (わかれる).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: The standard character form is 別れる. It means parting from a romantic partner or saying goodbye and going separate ways after a meeting.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse particle に with と when used with verb わかれる. わかれる must be used with と to indicate the person who is leaving together.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: The ramen at this restaurant is especially delicious.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun みせ that follows it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle の modifies noun ラーメン to show that the noodles belong to this restaurant.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle は marks ラーメン as the main topic being commented on or evaluated.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb comes before the adjective to emphasize that it stands out much more than other foods.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The い-ending adjective combines with です to form the predicate describing the topic's quality.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The noun phrase serving as the topic comes first with particle は. Then adverb とくに modifies the degree of adjective predicate おいしいです at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 特別[とくべつ]に means 'done in a special way / with special treatment', while とくに indicates that something stands out much more among other items.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Using とても only emphasizes the ordinary meaning 'very delicious' and does not suggest a strong comparison among the dishes.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Adverb とくに already contains the meaning 'especially', so it comes directly before an adjective or verb without needing another particle.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: I recommended a very interesting movie to my friend.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に indicates the person who receives information from the act of recommending.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The い-ending adjective in its basic form comes before and modifies noun えいが.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks えいが as the direct object affected by the act of recommending.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The する verb is in the polite past form した and serves as the predicate ending the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The structure expresses giving information or an object (N を) to the recipient (N に), ending with the verb meaning 'recommend' in the polite past form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 教える means giving instructions or passing on information, such as directions or a phone number. It does not imply recommending something good, as しょうかいする does.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 案内する means leading someone or giving a practical tour at a location, not recommending a work or an event.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: When recommending something to someone, the recipient always takes particle に (友だちに). Avoid confusing it with particle と.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: You do not need to write your name.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the object affected by the act of writing.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb directly modifies the noun ひつよう that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun combines with particle は to state the object being negated.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Verb あります takes the negative form to complete the structure meaning 'not necessary'.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: Verb かく stays in the dictionary form to modify noun ひつよう and combines with negative phrase はありません to express that something does not need to be done.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses a prohibition: writing is not allowed, rather than being unnecessary.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Expresses permission not to write, in an equivalent conversational style.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Do not change the verb before ひつよう into the て form or the past form when expressing that something does not need to be done.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + 必要がある/必要はない
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: This room is getting cold, isn't it?
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun meaning 'room' that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は makes the room the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The intransitive verb ひえる in the polite form combines with final particle ね to seek agreement about the temperature falling.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: The room is identified by demonstrative この and made the topic with は. The predicate uses intransitive verb ひえる to describe the temperature falling and ends with particle ね to seek agreement.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Use an adjective to describe the speaker's direct feeling of cold, instead of the process of the temperature falling.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Use a transitive verb meaning that the speaker actively makes the room cold.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse intransitive verb ひえる (become cold) with transitive verb ひやす (make something cold).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は marks the speaker as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun combines with copula です to serve as the predicate describing marital status.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: This is a basic noun judgment sentence. The topic わたし takes particle は, and the predicate is noun どくしん combined with polite final particle です.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses the same meaning, 'not married', but uses the negative form of a state verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Refers to being alone or by oneself, not specifically to marital status.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: The word どくしん is a noun, so it combines directly with です and does not change its ending like an adjective.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: There are many people in the classroom.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the place where something exists.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A quantity noun combines with the particle の to modify the following noun for people.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject as the people who exist.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: A verb that expresses the existence of people.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The classroom, which is the location, comes first with the particle に. Next comes the noun phrase functioning as the subject with the particle が, followed by the predicate verb います, which expresses the presence of people.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the adverb たくさん to commonly indicate that there are many people.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Place おおぜい as an adverb after the particle が to modify the verb directly.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: When おおぜい comes before a noun to modify it, the particle の must be added.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: My younger brother was very happy.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the younger brother the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the following verb meaning “to be happy.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb よろこぶ is changed to the polite past form to describe the emotional reaction of a third person.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The third-person topic おとうと combines with the particle は. Its degree is modified by the adverb とても, and the past-tense verb よろこぶ describes an observable emotional expression from another person.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The adjective うれしい is usually used to directly express the speaker’s own inner feelings.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a current happy state instead of an action that has already occurred.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Avoid directly using the adjective うれしい in a simple statement about another person’s feelings. Use the verb よろこぶ instead.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The first element in a compound noun referring to an upcoming period of time.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The second element means to come or arrive in the future.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: The word 「しょうらい」 is a time noun. It can function as an adverb or be used with 「の」 to talk about the speaker’s future plans.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: When 「未来」 is used, it usually refers to the distant future of society or science and technology, not to personal plans.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: When 「今度」 is used, it refers to the next time or the near future in everyday life.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 「将来」 (personal or career future) with 「未来」 (the distant future of humanity or society).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: On days off, I always help my mother cook.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the day off is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action 手伝います and shows its frequency.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who performs the cooking action in the modifying clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the clause 料理をする into a noun, and を marks the activity that the speaker helps with.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 料理をするの is nominalized to function as the object of 手伝います. 母が is the person who cooks, while the speaker is the implied subject of 手伝います.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Without 母が, the sentence only says that the speaker helps with cooking and does not clearly state whom they help.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: こと also nominalizes a clause, but it has a more formal and general meaning than の.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse 母が and 母を. In this sentence, the mother is the person who cooks, so use が, while the cooking activity goes with を.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: I want a light and sturdy bicycle.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い changes to かるくて to connect it to the next characteristic.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な comes before the noun 自転車 and keeps the form な.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the desired object with ほしい.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ほしいです expresses the desire to have an object.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: The two qualities, lightness and sturdiness, both modify the bicycle. Therefore, the first characteristic is connected with て, and the second characteristic comes directly before the noun. With ほしい, the desired object usually goes with が.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Nを買いたいです, the sentence emphasizes the desire to carry out the action of buying.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ほしそうです is used, it means that someone appears to want to have something. It does not directly state the speaker’s desire.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use を with ほしい in the basic pattern. The desired object usually goes with が.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q10.kobun.cn: Aいくて ＋ Aなな ＋ Nがほしいです
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: A: The restaurant is closed, isn’t it? B: Yes. But it will probably open soon.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This symbol opens speaker A’s dialogue.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject as being in the closed state.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: しまっています expresses a state in which something has closed and remains closed, while ね is used to confirm this with the listener.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ええ is an agreeing reply in conversation.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: でも connects a contrasting idea to the statement that the restaurant is closed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: This phrase refers to a very near time when the action of opening will occur.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: でしょう is attached to the plain form to express a mild prediction.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The first sentence states the restaurant’s current condition and uses ね to confirm it together. The second sentence changes direction with でも and places もうすぐ before the verb to predict that the restaurant will open soon.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vるはずです, the speaker confidently states, based on evidence, that the restaurant will certainly open.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If かもしれません is used, it only states a possibility, with a lower level of certainty than でしょう.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Learners may understand しまっています as currently carrying out the act of closing. In this sentence, it mainly indicates the state of being closed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.tokens.3.m: close, be in a closed state
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.tokens.12.m: suitable word or phrase to fill in
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ でしょう
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I slept for only three hours.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Quantity しか ＋ Vませんでした
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes yesterday the topic for talking about the length of sleep.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: しか limits the duration to three hours and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ねませんでした is the polite past negative form, completing the pattern しか + negative.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: きのうは states the time, ３時間しか limits the number of hours slept, and ねませんでした takes a negative form to complete the meaning “only.” In English, the sentence is translated as an affirmative statement, but Japanese still uses a negative form after しか.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: だけ also means “only,” but it does not have to be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: ぐらい means about three hours and does not emphasize the small amount as strongly as しか.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Learners may incorrectly use しか with an affirmative predicate. しか always needs to be used with a negative form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q12.kobun.cn: N ＋ しか ＋ Vない・Vません
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi: So that my mother would not scold me, I ate all the fish I disliked.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.vi: so as not to be scolded
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vないように expresses the purpose of avoiding something undesirable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before the noun 魚 to modify 魚.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the food that receives the action 食べる.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 全部 modifies the action of eating and shows that all the fish was eaten.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 食べる is in the polite past form and functions as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 母にしかられないように comes first to express the purpose of avoiding something. Then, きらいな魚を is the object of 食べました, while 全部 adds the degree to the action of eating.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ために emphasizes the purpose, but it is less natural than ように when talking about avoiding a situation.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: ような must come before a noun, so it cannot directly replace ように in this structure.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を by mistake after 母, but the person carrying out the action in a passive sentence usually goes with に.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi: Because I am not feeling well, please let me take tomorrow off.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the condition 悪い.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I am not feeling well
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a reason to the result or request in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes tomorrow the topic of the request.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.vi: please let me take the day off
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 休ませてください is a way to ask for permission or request that the listener allow the speaker to take the day off.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: The clause ぐあいが悪いので gives the reason first and then makes the request. The causative form 休ませてください expresses a request to someone with authority to allow the speaker to take the day off.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: から also indicates a reason, but it is usually more direct and subjective than ので in a polite explanation.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: 休んでください tells the listener to take a break, while 休ませてください asks someone else to allow the speaker to take a break.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 休ませてください as taking a break by oneself, but the causative form + てください means asking for permission to do something.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので／V使役形 + てください
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi: I do not have any brothers or sisters, but since I got a pet, I am no longer lonely.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that I am the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks what is being discussed in a pattern that expresses existence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: いません expresses that a person or animal does not exist; が connects to a mild contrast.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object of the action かう.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてから indicates the point after an action has been completed; は emphasizes the period starting from that point.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective い changes into the form く and combines with なる to express a change of state.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: The first clause describes the situation of having no brothers or sisters. Then, が creates a shift to the new result. かってからは identifies the point of change, while さびしくなくなりました expresses that the state of being lonely has ended.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Vたあとで indicates that one action happens after another, without emphasizing a state beginning from that point as てからは does.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: さびしくありません only says that the person is not lonely now, while さびしくなくなりました emphasizes the change from being lonely to not being lonely.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the adjective い into the form く before なる, so they may say さびしいなくなりました.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q15.kobun.cn: Vて形 + から（は）／Aい語幹 + く + なる
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: Mr./Ms. Suzuki is both intelligent and good at sports.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that 鈴木さん is the topic being described.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: も replaces が and shows that having a good mind is also an added advantage.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: し connects the first advantage to the following information and has a listing meaning.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: も marks sports as an additional area in which Suzuki is capable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: し connects two positive features to list several advantages of 鈴木さん. も is repeated to emphasize that both being intelligent and having sports ability are true.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: て connects features more naturally, while the listing nuance of several reasons in し is weaker.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: が expresses contrast or a change of topic, so it is less suitable than し when you only want to add another advantage.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate も simply as “also,” but they may forget that も can replace が or を and must be understood according to the noun before it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + し
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: I am about to go to the supermarket.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.sk: Time へ + N 辞書形 + Vところです
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the time when an action is about to begin.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: へ marks the direction of movement to the supermarket.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 行く modifies ところ and identifies this as the time just before going.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: V辞書形 + ところです expresses an action that is about to begin.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: 行く in the dictionary form comes before ところ to modify ところ. The pattern 行くところです identifies an action that has not started but is about to happen.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes an action happening at the moment of speaking, not one that is about to begin.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes an action that has just been completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 行くところです for “be going”; in fact, 行くところです means “be about to go,” while “be going” is usually expressed with 行っているところです.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: After leaving the house, I realized that I had forgotten something.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place being left in the phrase 家を出る.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Vてから connects leaving the house with the action that happens afterward.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object that the speaker realizes or notices.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 気がつく is a fixed verb phrase meaning to realize or notice.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The clause 家を出てから comes first to indicate the earlier time. In the phrase 気がつく, 忘れものに is the object realized, so に is used.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means “after leaving the house,” but it emphasizes the order of events rather than the direct connection as てから does.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning changes to “before leaving the house,” which is the opposite of the order in this sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 忘れもの, but 気がつく goes with に to mark what was realized.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: Please show me how to write Chinese characters.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 漢字 with 書きかた and shows whose writing method is meant.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 書きかた is a noun meaning writing method, and を marks the content for which guidance is requested.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: 書きかた is formed from the verb stem 書き and かた and means writing method. This phrase is the object of 教えてください, while の identifies the Chinese characters being discussed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This is also a request, but it is softer and takes the form of asking someone else to do it for you.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning changes to “I do not know how to write Chinese characters,” so it does not directly ask someone else to teach you.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake かた for a separate word; here, 書き + かた forms the noun “writing method,” and the verb before ください must be in the て form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + かた; Vて + ください
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: Please take this medicine when you are in pain.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the type of medicine whose use is being explained.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ときに indicates the time or situation when the medicine should be taken; いたい modifies とき.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 飲んでください is a polite request or instruction at the end of a sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: いたいときに is placed before the main clause to state the condition for the time of taking the medicine. The verb 飲む changes to the て form and combines with ください to create a polite instruction.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: は emphasizes the specific situation “when in pain,” with a sense of stating a rule or making a contrast.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: たら expresses the condition “if you are in pain,” focusing more on an assumption than on a time.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use いたいですとき; before とき, the direct modifying form いたいとき must be used.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ときに
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: I already asked Mr. Tanaka. I hear that he is free tomorrow.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person who was asked for information.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 聞きました is the verb 聞く in the polite past tense.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes tomorrow the topic of the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ひまだ is the adjective な in the plain form, used to connect with そうだ.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです indicates information heard from another person.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: The person who provided the information is marked by に, followed by the past action of asking. The topic of tomorrow comes before the state of being free, and then そうです shows that this is reported information.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: When used after the stem form ます of a verb or adjective, this pattern means “seems,” not “I hear that.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with らしいです still means “I hear that” or “seems,” but the sense of inference is stronger.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse そうです “I hear that” with そうです “seems”; look at the form of the word before it to tell them apart.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.tokens.9.m: I hear that it is so
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: Those two people got married just last month.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Vた + ばかりです
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 二人 is a noun meaning two people, and は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to show when the event happened.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: けっこんした is the verb “to get married” in the plain past form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ばかりです is attached after a past-tense verb to express that an event happened just recently.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, and “last month” adds the time of the marriage. Vたばかり emphasizes that the action is still recent at the time of speaking.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vたところです, it means that the action was completed just before speaking, so the time is even more recent.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The past form ばかりでした places the recent event at a past point in time.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use ばかりです directly after the dictionary form; this pattern requires the verb in the Vた form.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: A: Which hat is suitable? B: The red one is suitable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This symbol opens speaker A's dialogue.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the item being asked about in a question involving a choice.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: いいですか creates a polite question about which choice is suitable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: This symbol starts a new line and opens speaker B's dialogue.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: の replaces the noun ぼうし, while が marks the selected choice.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: いいです expresses that the choice is considered suitable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The question uses が to mark the choice that needs to be identified. In the answer, 赤いの is a shortened form of 赤いぼうし, which avoids repeating the noun already mentioned.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nが好きです, it means liking that hat, not necessarily choosing it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Using Nにします expresses the decision to choose the hat, which is stronger than saying that the choice is suitable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の in 赤いの; here, の replaces the noun ぼうし that was already mentioned.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: Aい・Aなな・Nの + のがいい
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: I have been made to eat curry every day, and I am getting fed up with it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing the time and repeated frequency of an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of eating.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The causative-passive verb form shows that the speaker is forced to do something they do not like.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle ばかり combines with で to state the reason for the unpleasant condition in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending な changes with the particle に to modify the verb なります, which shows a change in feelings.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate is in the polite form ます and ends the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The sentence combines the causative-passive form (食べさせられる - being made to eat) with the pattern 「〜ばかりで」 to express frustration when an annoying action keeps happening and leads to the negative result of becoming fed up.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「食べてばかりで」 (the active form) is used, it means that the speaker personally keeps eating only curry, not that someone forces them to eat it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「〜ばかりいる」 is used at the end of the sentence, it only describes an action that continues repeatedly; it does not function as a conjunction showing a reason (で) as it does in the original sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the causative-passive form (V-させられる: be made to do) with the simple passive form (V-られる: be done to or be given).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: Vて形・N + ばかり（だ / で）
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: Even if my parents oppose me, I still intend to study abroad.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the agent who performs the action in a passive sentence (受身).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 反対する changes to the passive form て + も to express a concessive condition (even if ... still).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the formal noun つもり.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The sentence-ending grammar pattern expresses the speaker's firm intention or plan.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses the passive form with the concessive particle 〜ても to state an obstacle. The second clause uses 〜つもりです to affirm the determination to act despite the opposition.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Changing to this expression for an objectively scheduled plan removes the personal determination expressed by つもり.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a simple hypothetical condition (if I am opposed...), without the concessive sense of acting despite something, as in ても.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the agent causing the action must be used with the particle に (両親に); do not use が or を.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q2.kobun.cn: Vて形・Aいくて・Aな/Nで + も ｜ V辞書形/ない形 + つもりだ
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: I used to hate bananas, but now I have become able to eat them.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states a past time point to emphasize the contrast with the present.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な changes to the informal past form だった and combines with けれど to connect two contrasting clauses.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が indicates the object receiving the ability when used with a potential-form verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 食べる changes to the potential form (食べられる) to show a newly gained ability.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The grammar pattern 〜ようになる expresses a change in a state or ability over time.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The first clause uses は to contrast the past and the conjunction けれど to create an opposition. The second clause uses a potential-form verb with 〜ようになる to express the change from “unable to eat” to “able to eat.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It only expresses the speaker's personal decision to eat, and does not show a change in ability like ようになる.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a firm judgment based on evidence, not an actual change of state.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: When a verb changes to the potential form (食べられる), the object particle を often changes to が (バナナが).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形/可能形/ない形 + ようになる
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: This is a cake made by my older sister, who is very good at cooking.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が indicates the object evaluated with the ability adjective 上手.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な directly modifies the noun 姉 that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the action 作った in the relative clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The past-tense verb 作った modifies the head noun ケーキ.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The noun combined with です acts as the main predicate and ends the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + N (relative clause 連体修飾節)
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: The sentence has two nested levels of relative clauses: the phrase “料理が上手な” modifies “姉,” and the whole clause “料理が上手な姉が作った” modifies the head noun “ケーキ.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect because in a clause modifying a noun (連体修飾節), the subject of the action must use が (or の), not は.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Changing to the dictionary form 作る would describe an action that has not happened yet or a habit, which is unsuitable because the cake has already been finished.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: In a relative clause modifying a noun, the subject performing the action must use the particle が, not the particle は.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi:
A: “Have you bought a birthday present for the department manager yet?”
B: “Yes. I have decided to give him the kind of alcohol the department manager likes.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This begins speaker A's dialogue. The noun combines with the particle の to modify お誕生日.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun with the honorific prefix お- combines with の to modify プレゼント.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the gift the main topic of the question.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing that an action has been completed by the present time.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite past predicate combines with the question particle か to end A's question.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: B's speech begins with a word showing an affirmative reply.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The subject in the relative clause modifying the noun お酒.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: This adjective ending な comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action さしあげる.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.9.n: The humble form of あげる (to give to a superior), in dictionary form, modifying the formal noun こと.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.10.n: The polite past grammar pattern 〜ことにする expresses the speaker's own decision.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: B uses the relative clause '部長が好きなお酒' as the object and combines the humble form さしあげる with the pattern 〜ことにする. This both shows respect for the superior and clearly states B's own decision.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the ordinary verb for giving instead of the humble form さしあげる is impolite when the receiver is a superior (部長).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Change it to ことになる when the decision was arranged by circumstances or an organization, not decided by B personally.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Distinguish 〜ことにする (the speaker's own decision) from 〜ことになる (a group decision or a decision caused by outside circumstances).
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形/ない形 + ことにする
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.sk: Time + N を + Vました
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is an adverb showing the time when an action happens.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb 食べました.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べました is the polite past form of the verb 食べる.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: きのう comes at the beginning of the sentence to state the time. It is followed by the object （牛肉）を and the action 食べました. The particle を connects the noun to the verb and shows what was eaten.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べていました, the sentence emphasizes an action that was in progress or happened regularly in the past.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse を with が because を marks the food that was eaten, not the person who performed the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: At present, I still cannot write difficult Chinese characters.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: むずかしい modifies かんじ, showing that they are difficult Chinese characters.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the Chinese characters as the object of writing.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns かく into a noun meaning the act of writing, while は makes the whole phrase the topic.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ modifies むりです, showing that it is still not possible at present.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: むりです serves as the predicate at the end of the sentence and says that the action is beyond the speaker's present ability.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: むずかしい modifies かんじ, and then かんじを makes it the object of かく. The phrase かくのは turns the act of writing into the topic. Then むりです states that this action is still impossible at present.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことは is used, the basic meaning is still “writing,” but the tone is more objective and formal than のは.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with かけません, the sentence directly says “cannot write,” focusing more on the speaker's ability than on judging the action as むり.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that のは must come after a verb in dictionary form to turn the whole action into the topic.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のは + N/Aなです
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: There are rare animals in my country.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the noun くに to show possession.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: には marks the place where something exists and makes the location a secondary topic.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective comes before どうぶつ to modify this noun.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists at the stated location.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: います is a predicate showing that a person or animal exists.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: The existence pattern places the location first with には, then states what exists with が. めずらしい comes directly before どうぶつ to limit the type of animals being discussed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used, the sentence must refer to objects or non-living things, not animals.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: で marks the place where an action happens, while には in this sentence marks the place where something exists.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use でいます. In a pattern showing that a person or animal is somewhere, use location + に + います.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: There is a very appealing smell.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.sk: Aい omit い + そうな + N が + します
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: そうな comes after an adjective to modify the noun におい, expressing the appearance or impression that it seems delicious.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks におい as the subject in the pattern においがする.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: する in においがする expresses sensing or giving off a smell.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます・ Aい omit い・ Aな omit な + そうだ; before a noun, use そうな.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: おいしそうな modifies におい, forming the phrase “a smell that seems delicious.” The pattern においがする uses が to mark the smell that is sensed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It means that the smell is truly delicious or pleasant, which is a more direct statement than おいしそうな.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Do not add な after おいしい before そう. Remove い and then add そうな.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: Because I overslept, I ended up being late for the exam.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The て form connects a cause or an earlier action to the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination or object toward which the action おくれる is directed.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてしまいました describes a completed action and often includes regret or an unintended result.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; the polite past uses Vてしまいました.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: ねぼうして states the cause first, and then に marks being late for the exam. しまいました emphasizes that the event happened unintentionally and was regrettable.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It only says that the speaker was late, without emphasizing regret as in おくれてしまいました.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use を with おくれる when saying that someone is late for a place or event; use に.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: After seeing the news about the accident, I was very surprised.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This noun phrase is the object of 見て, while を marks the whole content being watched.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of watching with the feeling that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: びっくりする is a verb showing an emotional reaction; the form しました describes an event that has happened.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: じこのニュースを is the content being watched, and を marks the object. 見て connects the earlier action with the びっくりしました reaction.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means “after watching,” but it emphasizes the time after the action more clearly.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: When 見る is used with specific content, Vietnamese learners may easily forget the particle を.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: Because I am busy, I still cannot manage to check my email.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.sk: Aい omit い + くて + なかなか + N が + Vできません
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い changes to the くて form to connect the cause to the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: なかなか is used with a negative sentence to express that something is difficult to do or has still not been achieved.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks checking email as an action that can or cannot be done.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: できません is the polite negative form of できる, expressing the inability to perform an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.cn: Aい omit い + くて; なかなか + negative predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: いそがしくて states the cause, while なかなかできません expresses that the action is difficult to do over a long period. が marks the action being described as impossible.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It means being unable to do something often or being unable to do much, with a weaker meaning than “still cannot do it.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Do not connect the adjective い with で. Change い into くて.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: Besides my friends, the teacher will also come to the party.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: いがいに means outside or besides the stated object.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle も adds the teacher as another participant in the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place or event that someone will go to.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: きます is the polite form of 来る and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: 友だちいがいに limits the scope of comparison, meaning outside friends. 先生も is the added subject, while パーティーに indicates the place or event that the teacher will come to.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means besides N and is usually neutral, with a meaning close to N以外に.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: も does not only mean “also”; it also replaces は or が to add another subject.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: Transportation in this area is very inconvenient.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes このあたり the topic being commented on.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks transportation as the thing being evaluated as inconvenient.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な serves as the predicate and ends with です in polite speech.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: このあたりは presents the place as the topic, while こうつうが is the content being commented on. ふべんです concludes the description of transportation in that area.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means that transportation in this area is inconvenient, but は shifts the focus to transportation itself.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: In a sentence evaluating one part or feature of the topic, が usually marks the thing being commented on, not は.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: Because I will meet a friend at 10 o’clock, I am getting ready to go out.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the meeting will take place.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who participates with someone or the person they meet.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason clause to the result that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies じゅんび and creates the meaning “preparations for going out.”
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object of します.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: します is the main predicate and describes carrying out the preparations.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The clause with から comes first to state the reason, while the action to be done comes after it. でかける modifies じゅんび, so it is placed directly before this noun.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので makes the reason sound softer and more objective.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: ために expresses a purpose or reason in a more formal way, rather than simply connecting a reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put から after the whole sentence or forget that the reason clause must come before the result.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Vます形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: Because the luggage is heavy, my arm hurts.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that has the feature of being heavy.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: おもい changes to おもくて to connect the reason with the pain in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: いたい is an adjective that dなescribes the state of the arm.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The adjective おもい is connected using the form て to state the reason leading to the state いたい. Each clause has its own subject, so both use が.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and directly.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the sentence sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.goukakumoshi3_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use おもいで instead of おもくて; the adjective い must change い to くて.
